methodology.review_method: AI source-context annotation and literal source validation; no human validation.
methodology.indexing: Zero-based eligible_corpus.json paragraph indices; source-record text cross-check. Full question fragments, exact selected evidence, answer paragraphs and character offsets retained.
methodology.episode_unit: A substantive question plus its answer, or local opening/speech passage. Question completions, short interjections, and editorial interruptions do not automatically split an answer. Substantive follow-ups do. Documents may contain several episodes.
methodology.prompting: Primary follow_up category retains independent direct-target vs topical targeting. Oral openings/speeches and voluntary pivots in other-topic answers both classify unsolicited_oral, with separate setting and pivot flags. Unsolicited means no relevant immediate question, not proof of unrehearsed or psychologically spontaneous speech.
methodology.sequence: favorable_before is before first selected criticism; favorable_between is interleaved; favorable_after is after last. Broader after-first boolean must not be described as a closing praise pivot. Same-answer findings exclude material in a different answer. Speeches are labeled local passage rather than answer.
methodology.favorable_language: Categories retain affinity, trust, conduct/competence appraisals, peace intent, defense/excuse, undercut niceness, and other qualifications separately. Conservative affirmative flag excludes solely pleasant call ratings, reported claims, disconfirmed trust, inferred relationships, picture courtesy, and generic other-actor blame. A favorable remark is not necessarily moral praise. Exact broad candidates remain inspectable.
methodology.classification_history: Original 42 clear/8 contextual/26 separate records retained. Independent explicit amendment of 202600046 from separate to clear yields current 43/8/25. See putin_negative_original76_amendments.json. All 76 must not be described as criticism.
methodology.limits: Selected official subset only; not exhaustive new frequency analysis and not social-media analysis. No population-level exposure denominator, no inference of fear, avoidance, external leverage, or intent.

part_methods.scope: First 38 prior negative-coded official records. Episodes anchor prior candidate evidence and additional criticism observed within those answer contexts; not an exhaustive new all-Putin corpus scan.
part_methods.unit: Answer-turn episode; short affirmations, question completions, and editorial interruptions may be grouped; substantive follow-up question starts a new episode. Speech/opening episode covers relevant contiguous oral remarks.
part_methods.order: Phrase character offsets in corpus paragraphs identify before/after order. Favorable_before is before first critical/candidate phrase; favorable_between is interposed between first and last; favorable_after is after last. The separate favorable_after_first_candidate is broader. These fields distinguish interposed affinity from an ending pivot.
part_methods.sentiment: Undercut pleasant-conversation rhetoric, disconfirmed trust, reported Putin claims, courtesy about a photograph, and other-actor blame are not automatically affirmative praise/excuse. The favorable markers retain broad candidates but explicit endorsement booleans allow conservative counts.
part_methods.trigger: follow_up is exclusive primary category plus independent question_targeting; direct_target_question names Putin or unambiguously references him. Topical questions about Russia/Ukraine are separate. Unsolicited in speech/opening differs from unsolicited pivot within an unrelated-topic answer.
part_methods.limitations: AI annotation, no human validation. All quotes literal-checked in cached eligible_corpus and source text; no claims about motive, fear, avoidance, or causal explanation. Oral unsolicited does not prove unrehearsed/spontaneous. Prepared_written reserved for actual written statements.

part_methods.scope: Last 38 records (original combined rows[38:]) in putin_negative_reaudit_combined.json, with prior selected passages and separately flagged additional context episodes. This is not a 76-criticism denominator or exhaustive corpus frequency estimate.
part_methods.classification: direct_target_question: question names Putin or uses an unambiguous Putin antecedent. topical_question_without_target: relevant Russia/Ukraine topic without personal Putin targeting. follow_up: substantive continuation of an earlier question/answer; separate targeting field retains directness. unsolicited_oral: no reporter question, or Putin introduced within an answer to an unrelated question (explicitly flagged). prepared_written reserved for genuinely written material; none in this slice. unclear reserved for missing/inadequate prompt context. Multipart question continuations separated by acknowledgment are not automatically substantive follow-ups.
part_methods.question_evaluation: criticism only when the wording expressly solicits a negative judgment or assent (e.g. disappointed, mad, wrong, less trustful, concerned about buying time); open_evaluation for open comparative or feelings questions. A factual/strategy question naming Putin is not by itself an express request for criticism.
part_methods.answer_boundaries: Substantive other-speaker questions end the preceding answer, even within the same topic. Short acknowledgments, inaudible interjections and unfinished attempts may be passed over if the answer demonstrably continues. Oral speeches are annotated as local topical passages, not as one answer spanning an entire document; no claim that they were improvised or prepared.
part_methods.favorable_sequence: Only same-answer/local-passage Putin language is marked. Before precedes the first substantive candidate-negative span; after follows the last; between is interleaved. Full paragraphs remain available through indices. Categories distinguish relationship claims, conditional praise, intent, competence and explanations/qualifications. Good relationship/call language is not equated with moral approval. Reported Putin praise of Trump, or praise of someone else, is excluded.
part_methods.limitations: AI source-context review, not human review. Prior labels are retained independently of prompting. Additional negative candidates are flagged, not silently pooled into prior-clear counts. No fear, avoidance, private motive or causal inference is made. Counts are descriptive of this selected audit set only.
part_methods.conservative_favorable_coding: All favorable-looking context remains quoted. The affirmative_favorable_or_excusing_endorsement flag is narrower: explicit current relationship, ability, constructive/peaceful intent, or character attribution. Undercut good conversations, positive meeting/call ratings alone, implicit favorable relationship, other-actor blame, generic minimizing/war explanations, and conditional would-look-great are not counted. Intent attributed by Trump is distinct from merely reporting Putin saying that he wants peace. Both broad context and conservative flags are available; neither proves motive.
part_methods.independent_episode_evaluation: Each episode is assigned clear/contextual/separate independently of the document’s immutable prior classification. Extra context candidates are flagged separately and do not automatically change prior record counts. Clear includes mild explicit disappointment and joint conduct/competence criticism as in the earlier audit; conditional and contextual limitations remain in the evidence and rationale.

summary.scope: Initiation and sequence annotation of the 76 originally negative-coded official records, with anchored episodes and clearly separated additional within-document context. No social posts are in this subset.
summary.not_population_rates: Counts describe a preselected candidate subset and source-context annotations. They do not establish rates per opportunity, silence/avoidance, relative treatment of other leaders, or motives. Additional clear episodes expand contexts within these records; they are not new documents unless an explicit record amendment says so.
